sentence_stem: If I had studied harder last year,
correct_completion: I would have passed the exam.
full_sentence: If I had studied harder last year, I would have passed the exam.
acceptable_variants: I would have got a better grade.
I would have been happier with the result.

options.text: I will pass the exam tomorrow.
options.why_wrong: This uses a future form with a time reference to tomorrow, but the stem describes a past hypothetical situation.

options.text: I pass the exam every year.
options.why_wrong: This describes a present habit and does not complete the imagined past result.

options.text: I would have passed the exam.
I would pass the exam now.
options.why_wrong: This uses a present-time result, which does not match the past condition introduced by 'last year'.

grammar_focus: Third conditional: if + past perfect, would have + past participle
explanation: The third conditional describes an imagined past situation and its imagined result. The past perfect follows 'if', and 'would have' plus a past participle goes in the main clause. Portuguese speakers often transfer a simple conditional form into this slot, but English requires the perfect structure for past hypotheticals.
translation: Se eu tivesse estudado mais no ano passado, eu teria passado no exame.
